note: Live-session recording of the screen scenes (series/tools/rec). prepare/teardown run on the laptop, not recorded; commands are typed and run for real. Servers are started hidden by prepare (helper %TEMP%\mgnet\svc.ps1) and their logs are shown with Get-Content/Select-String. Browser screens: use a clean/InPrivate window at 125 % zoom with DevTools docked right (Network, Disable cache). The 'Loading request ...' log line of the Web app is in %TEMP%\mgnet\ep06-web.log (tail it in a terminal beside the browser).

screens.name: interactive-server
steps: Open DevTools > Network, filter WS; hard reload (Ctrl+F5) http://localhost:5180/requests/2
Select the _blazor?id=... WebSocket and its Messages pane
In frame: '#2 · Data platform' and 'Rendered by: Server · interactive: True'
In a terminal beside it: Get-Content $env:MG_LOGS\ep06-web.log | Select-String 'Loading request' -> exactly one 'Loading request 2 from the API (Static)' for this page load
Click Approve: new WebSocket messages, status turns Approved, the buttons disappear

screens.name: webassembly
steps: DevTools > Network, filter All, Disable cache on; hard reload http://localhost:5180/requests/new

Show the _framework requests: dotnet.native.*.wasm, System.Private.CoreLib.*.wasm, ProjectRequests.Contracts.*.wasm, ProjectRequests.Web.Client.*.wasm; 'Rendered by' switches from Static to 'WebAssembly · interactive: True'
Clear the network log; type 49999 then 50000 in Budget: the preview flips Standard to High and the network log stays empty

Fill Title 'Laptop refresh', Requested by alex.demo@contoso.com, Department Finance, Budget 300000, no justification; Submit: 'A justification is required for budgets of 250,000 or more.' and still no request
Justification 'Replaces the 2019 fleet'; Submit: OPTIONS preflight then POST http://localhost:5207/api/requests (201), page shows 'Request #3 created · High priority.'

screens.name: cors-blocked
steps: The API was restarted by prepare with another allowed origin only (--Cors:AllowedOrigins:0=http://localhost:5999); show that command first in a terminal if wanted
Open DevTools Console + Network; submit a valid request on /requests/new

Console: "Access to fetch at 'http://localhost:5207/api/requests' from origin 'http://localhost:5180' has been blocked by CORS policy"; Network: the preflight without Access-Control-Allow-Origin; the page shows 'Could not reach the API: ...'
Restore: the teardown (or a re-run of prepare) restarts the API with the default origin; optionally submit again to show 201
